why: A second camera and a gimbal, so the picture and the strip can be photographed with
something on them (R-VID-14, R-VID-18, R-UI-12, R-UI-23).
**What it is for.** The gate's daemon is built from one camera answering no gimbal, and no
viewer ever reports to it, so eight rows of the blueprint manifest were built and
uncaptured: the state overlay on the picture (L-10 to L-13), which reaches a page only as
the daemon's answer to *that browser's own* viewer report; the drag hint (L-17), drawn only
where `aim` answers `present`; and the strip's `Still · N s` row, its thumbnail and its
`OTHER CAMERAS` figure (L-20 to L-22), which need a second camera that is running and has a
still to show. One camera and no gimbal can picture none of them.
**An overlay, not a second recording** — the shape `camera-sensor-turns.json` already has,
and for the same reason. `second` is copied from the recorded fixture's own `found[0]` on
the way past, changing only what a different socket changes: the `/dev` node, the by-path
name and the card. Keeping a whole second copy of eighteen recorded controls here would
drift from the board's the first time either was regenerated, silently.
`verify-pages.sh` is what merges the two.
**Nothing on the bench answers `aim`.** No gimbal has been attached to any board this
repository has run on, so `probeCamera` has never returned anything but `not-offered` for
it and there is no measurement to record. `aim` below is a shape a camera can have, not a
reading: the envelope is the one `present.test.ts` reasons about — both ends of both axes,
which is the only case `aimPanel` draws a gauge for — and the mode is the work mode such an
envelope would have been learned in. No page drawn from it may be reported as hardware
evidence.
**And the hint it puts on the picture has nowhere to send a gesture: K-62.** The drag layer
emits a slew per pointer move and `cam-pic-act`'s third output is wired to nothing, because
the daemon has no aim command route until the gimbal phase. Photographing L-17 here is a
picture of the affordance, and it is deliberately a picture of the open defect too — which
is better than the affordance being invisible to the gate while the defect stays open.
**Only the first camera carries the gimbal.** The second is the recorded camera exactly as
the board answered it, so the strip's two rows differ in what they are as well as in where
they are — and `capabilityFacts` still has a camera with `aim: none` to say so about.
**`second.camera` is the configuration entry, not a probe answer.** `verify-pages.sh` adds
it to the applied document through `POST /apply` like any other change and takes it out
again afterwards, so every other picture in the run is still of a one-camera board. Its
capture size and rate are the recorded camera's own, because they have to be a pair that
camera's `formats` offers — `refuse()` checks, and a start it refuses is a strip with
nothing running in it.
